target_customer: Home buyers and renters researching neighborhoods; no paying customer model found
problem: Movers had little easy-to-read data on crime, noise and prices of a neighborhood. Movity put local geodata on a map to help them choose.
business_model: free consumer data product with no revenue model found; acquired for team and technology

founders.name: Eric Wu
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later led Geo/Social Products at Trulia and later led Opendoor.

founders.name: Vaughn Koch
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CTO.

founders.name: Sha Hwang
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later led Geo/Social Products at Trulia and co-founded Nava.

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating and visualizing multiple geodata sets (crime, noise, prices) on interactive maps took some engineering and design skill, but was within reach of a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Built on public and licensed data sets that others could combine. Value was mostly in the team and visualization craft.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Trulia acquired Movity in December 2010 for its engineering team and data visualization expertise, per its later S-1.

market_need_then: Home search sites were adding neighborhood context in 2010, and Trulia bought the team for that capability. Direct evidence of user demand for Movity was not found.

branding.domain_note: movity.com is now used by an unrelated real estate careers site.
branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found. The team also ran the weeplaces.com check-in tracker.

brand_strength.rationale: Short-lived, no brand coverage found beyond the acquisition news.

outcome_analysis: Movity was a two to four person team that built neighborhood data maps, and Trulia bought it in December 2010, within a year of the batch, mainly for its engineers and visualization skills per Trulia's own S-1. The price was not disclosed. The founders went on to senior Trulia roles and later ventures such as Opendoor and Nava, so the outcome was an acquihire style landing rather than a scaled business.
notes: Funding is unverified: an aggregator (Kando/CB Insights style listing) shows a seed of about 1.3M and CB Insights shows 20K, and these conflict, so no round is recorded. Inman 2010 names the team without calling them founders; founder roles come from the YC page. Zain Memon appears on the Inman team list but not the YC page, so he is not listed as a co-founder. No competitors dated near the batch were found, so the list is empty. The acquisition is also confirmed by Trulia's S-1 (Dec 2010, for team and visualization expertise).
